This PostgreSQL parameter controls the cost assigned to a buffer cache miss during vacuum operations. Let me examine its characteristics: 1) It's a numerical parameter that accepts integer values, 2) Its default value is 2, 3) Valid range is typically 0 to very large positive integers, 4) When set to 0, it has a special meaning - it effectively disables the cost accounting for page misses during vacuum, making vacuum operations not count page misses toward the cost limit, 5) Values greater than 0 behave in the natural numerical order where higher values mean higher cost per page miss. Since setting it to 0 fundamentally changes the behavior (disabling cost accounting for page misses) rather than just being a lower cost value, this breaks the natural numerical ordering and constitutes special behavior.
